nodes.text: Hurst Publishers — review feedback
Hurst states that its scholarly books undergo rigorous anonymous peer review. This does not establish whether Sudden Justice underwent that procedure.
“Our scholarly books are subject to rigorous anonymous peer review procedures”

Hurst has published independently in London since 1969 and runs a specialist list in international affairs and conflict. Independence is the limit as well as the point: there is no peer review, and the prize shortlist printed on the publisher's own page could not be confirmed with the awarding body, so we do not rely on it. This record identifies the edition we cite so quotations can be traced; the weight sits on the book's own named interviews with pilots, analysts and commanders, not on its publisher.

Fixed in the revision reviewed on 6 October 2026. The named-editor error is corrected. Bill Roggio’s biography establishes the editorial attribution. Disclosed policy alignment remains a limitation; political admission alone does not prove an incident.
named editor
The biography identifies Roggio as the editor of FDD’s Long War Journal. This establishes a named editor, not a complete audit of corrections or editorial practice.

The Long War Journal is published by Public Multimedia Inc. as a project of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a think tank with a declared policy position, and it carries no masthead, named editor or corrections policy that we could find. The piece we cite is a named column republished from The Weekly Standard, which its own editor's note states. We use it for one narrow purpose, where its politics cut against the claim: it states that the CIA, with Pakistani and Saudi allies, did back Haqqani against the Russians, while rejecting the wider blowback argument in the same passage. A statement against interest is worth more than a friendly one.
